rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the eight-compound elution window and identify critical pairs while limiting run time. The low starting organic fraction preserves early retention, and the high endpoint reduces the risk of missing strongly retained compounds.

Halve the gradient slope while holding the solvent window and temperature fixed to test whether the crowded middle peaks and final coeluting pair respond to slope. This should also reveal a more precise elution window for subsequent targeted gradients.

Keep the improved gradient slope and raise temperature to test selectivity of the remaining near-coeluting pair. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, providing time headroom if further slope adjustment is needed.

Step temperature down to 55 C to improve the newly critical late pair while retaining most of the temperature-induced separation in the middle cluster. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate selectivity, with sufficient time margin below 10 minutes.

Return to the best temperature and make the gradient slightly shallower to test separation of its critical late pair. The previous last peak at 8.56 minutes leaves room for this adjustment without an expected time penalty.

The critical late pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so steepen beyond the best run to increase its separation and shorten elution. Check whether the middle pair, previously at R 1.61, retains adequate resolution.

Keep injection 6's gradient slope and temperature, but raise the starting organic fraction to perturb selectivity of the marginal R 1.46 pair. The first peak remains sufficiently retained to test this shift, which should also shorten the run.

Combine the higher starting organic fraction with a slightly shallower slope of 0.045 per minute to recover resolution in the middle cluster while preserving the improved late-pair separation. The endpoint remains above the observed elution window, so all peaks should elute during the gradient.

Injection 8 has reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark while testing a shorter elution window in time. Raise the starting organic fraction and modestly reduce the slope to compensate for compression of the middle cluster.

Lengthen injection 9's gradient by one step to improve its sole unresolved pair, monitoring the late pair at R 1.66 for a possible selectivity tradeoff. Retain injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark.

The 60 C refinements show competing resolution requirements, so test a cooler selectivity regime with a steeper gradient aimed at rapid elution. Injection 8 remains the established maximum-score method while this run explores an alternative route to full resolution.

Shorten the cool-temperature gradient by one step to test whether its near-coeluting middle pair separates on the steeper side of a selectivity crossover. This also tests a faster alternative while retaining injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Further steepening may separate the cool-temperature middle pair, while a modest temperature increase tests whether the marginal late pair can be improved simultaneously. This explores a faster alternative without displacing injection 8's established maximum score.

Test a steeper gradient at the lowest temperature to push the persistent middle pair farther from its apparent coelution region. Monitor the marginal late pair closely; injection 8 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to change middle-cluster selectivity while preserving separation of neighboring pairs. This explores a shorter fully resolved alternative; injection 8 remains the established maximum-score method.

Raise the starting organic fraction and slightly steepen injection 15's gradient to move its critical middle pair farther apart while shortening elution. Return to 30 C to preserve the better late-pair separation, retaining injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Lower temperature to improve injection 17's critical middle-cluster separation, and slightly flatten the gradient to protect the late pair that becomes marginal at 25 C. This targets full resolution near four minutes while retaining injection 8 as the proven maximum-score method.

Lower only the temperature from injection 19 to improve its sole unresolved middle pair, using the favorable cooler-temperature selectivity seen in injection 18. The late pair has substantial resolution margin, making this a promising faster fully resolved method.

Shorten injection 20's gradient by one grid step to seek faster elution while spending its resolution margin. Monitor the middle and late pairs for loss of baseline separation, retaining injection 20 as the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Use an intermediate slope between injections 20 and 21 by lowering the endpoint one step. This should recover the marginal middle pair while keeping elution faster than injection 20 and comfortably within the gradient.

Raise the starting organic fraction to accelerate elution, compensating with a shallower slope to protect the critical middle pair. Retain injection 22 as the fastest proven fully resolved method while testing this shifted solvent window.
